\begin{center}
{\LARGE Ridge Broker Ablation Experiment}
\end{center}
\vspace{0.75em}

\paragraph{Question and design.}
These \rav{nAblations} ablations restrict the broker's Ridge learning setup.
They are not an additive decomposition of its advantage. The base Ridge
reference pools mediated-match observations and uses additive and bilinear pair
features. \emph{Size-matched pooled history} retains those features but limits
the broker to the smaller of its available sample and the median agent fitting
sample. \emph{Single-principal history} randomly retains one endpoint type from
each mediated match. At prediction, its fitted one-type function scores both
parties, with the fitting-sample output mean subtracted once. \emph{Additive
Ridge} retains both endpoint types but replaces the pair features with their
type-vector sum. The latter two variants cannot represent bilinear interactions.
Agent parameters remain fixed, although matching can change agents' realized
histories. All conditions use $\lambda_a=\rav{ridgeLambdaAgent}$ and
$\lambda_b=\rav{ridgeLambdaBroker}$, the same fitting schedule, and the same
broker observation cap before size matching.

The primary estimand in realization $c$ is the late-period broker-minus-principal
difference in holdout rank correlation
\[
G_v(c)=\overline r_{b,v}(c)-\overline r_{a,v}(c),
\]
for Ridge broker variant $v$. The ablation contrast is
$G_v(c)-G_{\mathrm{pair}}(c)$. Each bar averages periods
\rav{latePeriodStart}--\rav{latePeriodEnd} within seed
and then averages seeds. The baseline comparisons use \rav{nBaselineSeeds}
common seeds. Other conditions use \rav{nOtherSeeds} common seeds. The
$\rho\times\delta$ analysis gives one observation to each of the
\rav{nConditions} effective realizations, including the baseline. Repeated
grid coordinates that map to the same realization receive no additional
weight. Because the ablations alter broker rankings, matches, and later
learning histories, the contrasts describe the resulting systems, not
fixed-data comparisons of fitted regressions.
